{{short description|Italian mathematician and academic}}
[[File:Caporaso lucia.jpg|thumb|Lucia Caporaso in [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]], 2006]]
'''Lucia Caporaso''' is an Italian mathematician, holding a professorship in mathematics at [[Roma Tre University]]. She was born in Rome, Italy, on 22 May 1965. Her research includes work in [[algebraic geometry]], [[arithmetic geometry]], [[tropical geometry]] and [[enumerative geometry]].

==Education and career==
Caporaso earned a [[laurea]] from [[Sapienza University of Rome]] in 1989.{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. at [[Harvard University]] in 1993. Her dissertation, ''On a Compactification of the Universal Picard Variety over the Moduli Space of Stable Curves'', was supervised by [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]].{{r|cv|mgp}}

She became a Benjamin Pierce Assistant Professor of Mathematics at Harvard, a researcher at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]], an assistant professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and an associate professor at the [[University of Sannio]], before moving to Roma Tre as a professor in 2001. From 2013 to 2018, she has headed the Department of Mathematics and Physics at Roma Tre.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Caporaso was the 1998 winner of the [[Bartolozzi Prize]].{{r|bart}}

She is an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking in the section on algebraic and complex geometry.{{r|icm}}
